overview: Pernod Ricard is the world's second-largest spirits and wine group, created by the 1975 merger of Pernod and Ricard, with FY2026 (ended 30 June 2026) consolidated net sales of EUR9,404 million. The Group owns more than 170 premium spirits and Champagne brands across every major category -- including Absolut vodka, Jameson Irish whiskey, Chivas Regal and Ballantine's Scotch, Martell cognac, Havana Club rum, Beefeater gin and Mumm/Perrier-Jouet Champagne -- distributed in over 160 countries. In FY2026 the Group reorganised its portfolio into two complementary Brand Units: a 'Gold' unit for aged, heritage spirits (whisky, Champagne, cognac) and a 'Crystal' unit for dynamic, non-aged, mixable spirits (vodka, tequila/mezcal, rum, gin, liqueurs, RTDs).

business_model.summary: Pernod Ricard makes money manufacturing, maturing, marketing and distributing branded spirits, wine and Champagne, captured through a 'grain to glass' value chain of owned distilleries, vineyards and bottling plants plus a route-to-market network of market companies and distributor partners. Growth is driven by premiumisation -- trading consumers up into higher price tiers -- supported by heavy advertising & promotion (A&P) spend (~15-16% of net sales) that builds brand equity and pricing power. Revenue is transactional (case/bottle sales to distributors, retailers and travel retail operators) rather than subscription-based, but demand is recurring and has historically been resilient outside of destocking cycles.

revenue_streams.name: Strategic International Brands (Absolut, Jameson, Chivas Regal, Ballantine's, Martell, Havana Club, Beefeater, etc.)
Strategic Local Brands (Royal Stag, Blenders Pride, Seagram's)
Specialty Brands (craft/agave/American whiskey/aperitifs - Bumbu, Codigo, Skrewball, Lillet)

business_model.customer_type: B2B route-to-market through distributors, wholesalers, retailers (off-trade), bars/restaurants (on-trade), travel retail operators and growing direct-to-consumer e-commerce; ultimate end consumer is B2C
business_model.geographic_mix: FY2026 net sales: Asia/Rest of World ~42% (China, India, Japan, Australia, Africa/Middle East, Turkiye), Americas ~27% (USA ~15%, Canada, Brazil, Mexico), Europe ~31% (France, UK, Germany, Spain, Poland); ~55% mature markets / ~45% emerging markets by FY26 net sales

main_competitors: Diageo (Johnnie Walker, Smirnoff, Guinness, Captain Morgan)
competitive_position.market_position: Second-largest global spirits company by sales behind Diageo, with ~5.9% global value share of total spirits retail sales (including RTD) as of 2025, up from 4.9% in 2020; #1 or #2 position in numerous categories including vodka (Absolut), Irish whiskey (Jameson), and Indian whisky (Royal Stag, the world's largest-selling whisky brand by volume)

moat_factors.description: Most diversified portfolio in the industry (170+ brands spanning every category and price tier from standard to ultra-prestige), reducing reliance on any single category or price point and allowing the Group to capture consumption occasions wherever they occur
Owned market companies in 60+ countries plus distributor network in 160+ countries gives real-time consumer insight and shelf/on-trade presence that smaller/local rivals cannot match

Decades-long maturation stocks (Scotch, cognac, rum) and controlled vineyards/distilleries in France, Mexico, China create a high barrier to entry and multi-year lead time that new entrants cannot replicate quickly
~15-16% of net sales reinvested in advertising and promotion sustains premium positioning, though this is being tested as consumers trade down
Balanced mature/emerging market exposure (55/45) cushions regional shocks, evidenced by Rest-of-World (Turkiye, India, Japan) growth partly offsetting US/China weakness in FY26

weaknesses: Heavy reliance on cognac (Martell) and Scotch/Irish whiskey for premium mix, categories hit hardest by Chinese anti-corruption/gifting curbs and US destocking

US market softness: FY26 USA net sales -14% amid distributor inventory adjustments and weak spirits category demand, with structural depremiumisation (consumers trading down) evident across the industry
China exposure (~8-9% of group sales) remains volatile: FY26 China net sales -19% amid weak consumer sentiment, tightened on-trade regulation and anti-dumping tariff uncertainty
Net debt of ~EUR10.7bn (Net Debt/EBITDA ~3.3x at FY26, 3.8x at H1 FY26 average-rate basis) constrains capital flexibility and dividend/buyback growth until deleveraging below 3x targeted by FY2029
Premiumisation thesis -- the core value-creation lever for a decade -- is being challenged by analysts (e.g., Euromonitor) as reaching structural limits rather than a cyclical pause

growth_drivers: Continued premiumisation in emerging markets: India (Royal Stag, Blenders Pride, Seagram's Xclamat!on) delivering FY26 net sales +7% on favourable demographics and a growing middle class
RTD (ready-to-drink) format expansion: +12% organic growth in FY26, broad-based across Canada, Australia and Western Europe, recruiting new/younger consumers
Structural demographic tailwinds: legal-drinking-age population growth (+1.2% CAGR to 2030 in emerging markets) and expanding middle class (+4% by 2030) per IWSR/OECD data cited in the FY26 URD
Operational Efficiencies programme: targeting EUR1 billion of savings from FY2026-FY2028 (half delivered in FY26), supporting margin defence amid soft top-line

Active portfolio management / M&A: continued pruning of non-core assets (Imperial Blue sale to Tilaknagar closed Nov 2025; Mumm Napa/US sparkling wine sale to Trinchero closed April 2026) to refocus capital on premium international spirits and Champagne, plus bolt-on innovation (Absolut Tabasco, Malibu Pink, Kahlua Dunkin', Lillet 0.0%)
Travel retail recovery: Global Travel Retail returning to growth with resumption of Martell sales in China Duty Free and international passenger traffic ~10% above pre-COVID levels
Non-alcoholic/low-ABV expansion (Lillet Blanc 0%, Almave minority stake) addressing moderation trend among younger consumers

business.risk: US spirits market softness and distributor destocking
business.description: FY26 USA net sales declined 14% (organic), with inventory adjustments expected to continue weighing on sales into FY27; broader US category is depremiumising as consumers trade down

business.risk: China demand weakness and regulatory tightening
business.description: FY26 China net sales -19%; tightened on-trade regulation, weak consumer/business sentiment, and cognac (Martell) particularly exposed to prestige-category pullback
Industry data (IWSR, Euromonitor) shows global spirits value declining and premium tiers (>$50, >$100) losing share to standard/value tiers for the first time in years
Multi-year channel inventory correction in China/US following pandemic-era overstocking has pressured Martell volumes (-12% organic FY26, -5% volume)
Growing bargaining power of large retail/distribution customers and craft/local competitors pressuring pricing and shelf space

financial.description: Net debt ~EUR10.7bn at FY26 year-end; Net Debt/EBITDA ~3.8x (H1 FY26 average-rate basis), above the long-term comfort zone; management targets below 3x only by FY2029

Adverse FX (USD, Turkish lira, Indian rupee, Chinese yuan) reduced FY26 reported net sales by a material margin versus organic growth (-14.2% reported vs -3.9% organic); limited natural hedging outside debt-currency matching
EUR216m unfunded pension obligations; 96% of debt is fixed-rate limiting direct rate sensitivity, but refinancing at higher rates could raise average cost of debt (currently ~3.2-3.4%) over time

regulatory.description: US tariff policy on EU-origin goods remains a live risk; CFO previously estimated a 10% US tariff on EU imports could cost Pernod ~EUR200m annually (about half offsettable via mitigation); Scotch whisky secured tariff-free treatment under a UK-US deal (announced July 2026), but Irish whiskey, Champagne and cognac exposure persists pending a broader EU-US spirits agreement

regulatory.risk: China anti-dumping duties on EU brandy/cognac
regulatory.description: China imposed anti-dumping duties of up to 34.9% on EU brandy from July 2025; Pernod Ricard, along with Remy Cointreau and Moet Hennessy, negotiated an exemption conditional on minimum resale pricing, but the overhang on cognac trade policy and the risk of future escalation remains

Excise tax increases (e.g., Poland, India's Maharashtra state) directly dampen volumes and distort trade phasing; rising global focus on public health/alcohol harm reduction could bring further duty increases
Increasing regulatory and societal scrutiny of alcohol marketing and advertising in various jurisdictions could constrain brand-building activities

macro.risk: Chinese consumer weakness and anti-corruption/gifting culture shift
macro.description: Sustained weak consumer and business sentiment in China, compounded by a multi-year anti-corruption/austerity campaign that has structurally reduced high-end gifting and on-trade entertaining occasions central to cognac and prestige whisky consumption

Trade wars (US-China, US-EU), the Russia/Ukraine conflict (~3% of pre-war sales), and the Q4 FY26 Middle East conflict disrupting sales in affected markets; inflation pressuring consumer discretionary spend globally
Rising health consciousness and claimed spirits moderation among younger generations (GenZ) is a structural headwind requiring portfolio adaptation (RTDs, 0% ABV variants)
Aged 'wet goods' (maturing spirits) inflation and glass/packaging costs pressured FY26 gross margin by ~70bps from tariffs and low-single-digit COGS inflation, partly offset by efficiency programmes

macro_factors.industry_outlook: Global spirits industry value growth has stalled: IWSR preliminary 2025 data shows total beverage alcohol value declined for the first time since 2020, with spirits particularly hard hit; the International Western Style Spirits (IWSS) segment Pernod focuses on had grown ~5%/year over the prior decade but premium tiers are now losing share to standard/value tiers in key markets like the US. Management and Euromonitor disagree on whether this is cyclical (destocking, macro softness) or structural (premiumisation plateauing)
macro_factors.cyclicality: Moderate-to-high in the near term - spirits are consumer discretionary and currently experiencing a pronounced destocking/demand air pocket in the US and China; historically more resilient than other discretionary categories due to brand loyalty and habitual consumption, but FY2025-26 has shown real volume and value declines
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: Low-to-moderate direct sensitivity (96% fixed-rate debt), but elevated net debt (~3.3-3.8x EBITDA) means refinancing costs and deleveraging pace are watched closely by rating agencies and the market
key_input_costs: Aged spirits inventory carrying costs ('wet goods')

recent_developments.event: FY2026 full-year results: net sales EUR9,404m (-14.2% reported, -3.9% organic), profit from recurring operations EUR2,423m (-17.9% reported, -5.2% organic), net profit EUR1,203m (-26%); shares fell ~6% on the day as sales missed consensus despite a margin/cost beat; FY27 guidance of broadly stable organic net sales seen by some analysts (AlphaValue) as lacking precision

Pernod Ricard welcomed confirmation of tariff-free Scotch whisky trade between the UK and US, while continuing to call for a broader US-EU spirits tariff agreement covering Irish whiskey, Champagne and cognac
Announced Mauve Croizat as new EVP Finance & Tech effective 1 October 2026, succeeding Helene de Tissot, who departed after 23 years to become Global CFO of Chanel
Closed sale of Mumm Napa, Mumm Sparkling California and DVX (US sparkling wine assets) to Trinchero Family Wine and Spirits, continuing the refocus on premium international spirits and Champagne
Closed sale of the Imperial Blue business division in India to Tilaknagar Industries, immediately accretive to margins and growth, freeing resources for premiumisation in India

H1 FY2026 results: net sales EUR5,253m (-14.9% reported, -5.9% organic); China -28% organic amid tightened regulatory environment and weak consumer sentiment; US -15% on inventory adjustments; Net Debt/EBITDA 3.8x (average-rate basis)

China concluded its anti-dumping investigation into EU brandy, imposing duties up to 34.9% from July 2025, but exempted Pernod Ricard (along with Remy Cointreau and Moet Hennessy) conditional on minimum resale pricing commitments

guidance.as_of: FY2026 Annual Results / Universal Registration Document (16 September 2026)

items.notes: Expected declines continuing in US and China in H1 FY27 due to inventory adjustments, offset by continued Rest-of-World growth (especially India); FY26 organic decline was -3.9%

items.target: Close to the lower end of +3% to +6% range
items.notes: Explicitly acknowledges 'current softness in the US market'; previously the medium-term range had been communicated without this lower-end qualifier
FY26 A&P ran at 15.0% of net sales (low end of range); management reaffirms consistent brand investment despite cost discipline elsewhere

items.target: Strong defence / expansion over medium term
items.notes: Supported by acceleration of the EUR1 billion Operational Efficiencies programme (from FY2026 to FY2028, half already delivered in FY26) and strict cost control

items.period: FY2027 and medium-term (normalizing to no more than ~EUR700m)
items.notes: Reflects normalization from previously elevated strategic investment levels to preserve cash generation
FY26 cash conversion improved +17pts to 91%, ahead of the ~90% target, via disciplined investment and working capital management
FY26 year-end net debt EUR10,662m; deleveraging trajectory supported by FCF growth and normalized strategic investment, but starting point (~3.3-3.8x depending on basis) requires sustained execution

guidance.management_commentary: Chairman & CEO Alexandre Ricard framed FY2026 as a year of 'disciplined execution defending margin, delivering efficiencies and strengthening cash generation' in a 'contrasted and uncertain environment,' citing resilience ex-US/China (+0.5% organic) and improving second-half momentum (H1 -5.9% organic vs H2 -1.3% organic). Management remains confident in long-term structural demand tailwinds (legal-drinking-age population growth, expanding middle class, premiumisation) while explicitly flagging continued US and China softness into FY2027 and a Q4 FY26 Middle East conflict impact expected to also weigh on Q1 FY2027.

bull_case: Unmatched brand and category diversification (170+ brands, Gold/Crystal Brand Units spanning every price tier) provides resilience and optionality that narrower rivals like Remy Cointreau (cognac-concentrated) lack

Sequential improvement already visible: organic sales trend improved from -5.9% in H1 FY26 to -1.3% in H2 FY26, and management guides to broadly stable organic net sales for FY27, suggesting the worst of the US/China destocking cycle may be passing
EUR1 billion Operational Efficiencies programme (half delivered in FY26, full delivery by FY28) is structurally improving the cost base and supporting margin defence even as top-line stays soft

Strong and improving free cash flow (EUR1,197m FY26, +6%, 91% cash conversion) funds continued deleveraging toward the <3x Net Debt/EBITDA target by FY2029 and should eventually re-enable more aggressive capital returns

Emerging-market structural tailwinds remain intact and are already showing through: India +7% organic FY26 (Royal Stag now the world's #1 whisky by volume), Turkiye +26% in FY26 becoming the Group's 4th-largest market, Japan +8%

Valuation has de-rated substantially (shares down from a 52-week high near EUR107-141 depending on source, to the EUR65-75 area) and several analysts (e.g., Citi, Barclays) maintain Buy/Overweight ratings despite cutting price targets, viewing the stock as cheap relative to normalized earnings power
bear_case: US destocking and depremiumisation may not be purely cyclical: industry-wide data (IWSR, Euromonitor) shows consumers structurally trading down and premium-tier value share shrinking for the first time in a decade, undermining the core premiumisation growth thesis

China remains highly unpredictable: a -19% organic decline in FY26 (after -28% in H1) reflects not just macro softness but a durable shift away from high-end gifting/on-trade entertaining tied to anti-corruption policy, with no clear catalyst for full recovery and cognac (Martell) especially exposed

Elevated leverage (~3.3-3.8x Net Debt/EBITDA) limits financial flexibility, and the FY2029 deleveraging target implies several more years of balance-sheet repair before capital return can meaningfully accelerate

Tariff and trade-policy overhang is unresolved: US tariffs on EU spirits (estimated ~EUR200m annual gross impact at a 10% rate) and China's anti-dumping regime on EU brandy (up to 34.9% for non-exempted players) both remain live risks that could re-escalate depending on US-EU and EU-China trade negotiations

FY27 guidance of 'broadly stable' organic net sales and a medium-term range guided to the 'lower end' of +3%-6% signals management itself lacks confidence in a sharp snapback, and several analysts (AlphaValue) flagged the FY27 outlook as imprecise and the US/China recovery as unconfirmed

Currency exposure (USD, Turkish lira, Indian rupee, Chinese yuan) continues to create a large gap between organic and reported results (FY26: -3.9% organic vs -14.2% reported net sales), adding volatility and reducing the predictability of reported earnings for investors
